title: Autonomy in medical rehabilitation
summary:
The autonomy of individuals with rehabilitation needs in medical rehabilitation is closely linked to the goals of self-determination and participation as defined in § 1 of the Social Code Book IX, as well as to the framework concept of the German Pension Insurance. The preservation and promotion of the autonomy of rehabilitation participants is crucial to ensuring self-determination and participation.
With this project, we aim to find out how self-determination of rehabilitation participants is currently implemented in inpatient rehabilitation facilities, what obstacles exist, and how we can overcome them. This also includes understanding what individuals mean by "autonomy."
First, we want to learn about the current state of autonomy, that is, self-determination, of rehabilitation participants in German rehabilitation facilities. To this end, rehabilitation facilities in Germany will be surveyed in writing. We want to know not only what is being done to maintain and promote the autonomy and self-determination of rehabilitation participants but also to inquire about challenges and obstacles.
In addition to the written survey, we will speak with practitioners in rehabilitation facilities as well as with rehabilitation participants to include their perspectives. For example, we want to know how self-determination is experienced in rehabilitation, what conditions promote self-determination, and what may be hindering it.
With the involvement of experts, recommendations for practice regarding the preservation and promotion of the autonomy of rehabilitation participants will be developed. This will support and promote the overarching goal of self-determination and participation for individuals with rehabilitation needs.
conditions: Orthopaedics, internal medicine/metabolic diseases, oncology, psychosomatics, cardiology, neurology

interventions.name: Rehabilitation patients with the six most common main indications (orthopaedics, internal medicine & metabolic diseases, oncology, psychosomatics, cardiology, neurology) are interviewed once by telephone between 45 and 60 minutes on their subjective perception of autonomy during rehabilitation.

Professionals (doctors, physiotherapists, exercise therapists, nutritionists, occupational therapists, psychologists, social workers, nurses) with at least 1 year of professional experience and working in the main rehabilitation indications mentioned are interviewed once by telephone for between 45

Heads of inpatient medical rehabilitation facilities are surveyed once online in writing on the current status of maintaining and promoting the autonomy of rehabilitants and on the needs of the facilities in this regard

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Rehabilitants:
-interview time after discharge from the rehabilitation clinic and a maximum of 4 weeks after the end of the rehabilitation stay
Rehabilitation stay in one of co-operation clinics
Rehabilitation programme in one of the above-mentioned main rehabilitation indications
-Written consent to the study

Professional group members:
-Rehabilitation practitioners in the above-mentioned professional groups
-employment in one of the above-mentioned co-operation clinics
-working in at least one of the above-mentioned main rehabilitation indications
-At least 1 year of professional experience in current position
-Written consent to the study

Rehabilitation institutions:
-Written consent to the study
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient knowledge of the German language
